summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-driven remote-shell agent under an httpx/requests typosquat name
details: The package name typosquats the popular HTTP clients httpx and requests, but its actual behavior — declared in METADATA as 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management' — is a remote-control agent. On import, __init__.py exposes `start_bot` from a Cython-compiled `bot` module which, together with compiled `handlers` and `core` modules and a dependency on python-telegram-bot, connects out to Telegram and dispatches incoming bot messages to shell execution on the installer's host. This is a network-to-shell control channel driven by whoever holds the embedded bot token, not by the installer. All logic is delivered as compiled.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so binaries with no Python source, and a dedicated `obfuscate` submodule exports `enc_b64` and `_xor` routines used to hide string constants (bot token, allowed chat_id, endpoint URLs) inside those binaries. Publisher metadata is unfilled placeholder text (`Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, homepage `github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), so there is no accountable maintainer. A developer who mistypes `httpx` or `requests` and installs this package obtains a persistent remote-shell backdoor on their machine controlled by the package author.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
